title: You win some, you lose some? #theatre #musicaltheatre
transcript: So I had a panic attack at the theatre yesterday, and it's no one's fault, really, except maybe partly my own. But I wanna talk about it because first of all, I was planning to review this show and now I don't really feel like I can. But also because I I think it speaks to one of the really tricky things about live theatre in general. The very unfortunate piece of context here is that this happened during a show called Animal Wisdom, which I literally listed in another video as my number one most anticipated show of 2026. Because it's written by Heather Christian, who I'm a really big fan of, this is a revival of a theatre piece based on her own experiences with ghosts and spirituality, using text and music with Southern Gothic gospel influences. Cool concept, very much up my alley. And the music was stunningly beautiful. But there was this very unfortunate cocktail of circumstances that individually might have been fine, but in combination, um, were just, like, really bad for me. I will say some of it stemmed from the show itself. Like, there's sort of is a plot, sort of isn't. It's more story driven than her other big show, oratorio for living things, which is, like, all concept and vibe. But I found that story kind of elusive and tough to latch on to. Especially because. And this is the first big thing on my end, I was kind of sleep Deprived and exhausted from work. So I was already in this, like, dazed, disoriented state. Just not in the right headspace for this kind of show, which was also, by the way, two hours and 10 minutes with no intermission. And I timed my bathroom trip before the show very poorly, so I, like, really had to go again. So I was physically uncomfortable in addition to being mentally uncomfortable. But then on top of that, the final 30 minutes or so of the show are done mostly in darkness, but with these, like, sudden and quick flashes of light and very loud music and drums. And they did warn us about this beforehand, and I just didn't think it would be a problem, cause I've done way more intense theatrical experiences than this. I did Viola's room and had no problem whatsoever. But all of it in combination, I just found to be a really unpleasant sensory experience. And so I started to get kind of panicky and claustrophobic. But the final kicker, and this is also maybe a bit of a criticism of the show, is that it kept seeming like it was going to end. each number in the final section felt like it could have been this grand finale, but it just kind of keeps going and going and going. And normally I could just laugh and be like, LOL, who hired Peter Jackson for this show? But in this context, it actually Started to really mess with my head and I started feeling like I maybe will never leave this theatre. The result of all of that is that I had a bit of a panic episode, mild enough that I could kinda keep it to myself to not bother the people around me, but then that also kinda made it worse. But even after all of that, I would still probably recommend the show to people because Heather Christian is a brilliant artist. I'm desperately craving this exact kind of avant garde alternative musical storytelling. I want more of it, I want people to support it. And even the specific things I found overstimulating might have been wildly exhilarating to me on a different day. And that's what's tricky but also kind of beautiful I guess, about live theatre, that you just literally have no choice but to meet it where you're at. It just sucks cause I was really looking forward to this show and now I feel like my perception of it is maybe forever tainted by these factors that were outside of their control.
classificationReason: Creator attended Animal Wisdom and offers some opinion ('music was stunningly beautiful'), but explicitly states they do not feel they can review it due to a panic attack they experienced. The video's primary purpose is discussing that personal experience, not reviewing the production. Does not qualify as a review.
